response.draft:
Slide 1: A Flight Enclosure for Ketterly County's Hawks and Owls
Bramblecote Wildlife Recovery
Request to the Harrow Valley Community Foundation, Environmental Stewardship Fund
$60,000 toward a $148,000 raptor flight enclosure and care project
Opening spring 2027 on our Mill Lane site
December 3, 2026

Slide 2: Thank You, and What This Request Is
Thank you for $50,000 in general operating support in FY2026
That grant kept our care staff, hotline, and clinic running through a record year
Today's request is separate: a one-time capital project, not operating support
Who we are: a licensed wildlife rehabilitation center on four acres north of downtown Ketterly
2.5 full-time care staff, a contract veterinarian two mornings a week, 97 volunteers
FY2026 revenue $428,900; expenses $412,600; $16,300 surplus added to reserves
87% of spending went to programs; reserve covers about 2.5 months of expenses

Slide 3: FY2026 at a Glance
1,611 animals admitted, up 41% from 1,142 in FY2024
117 species treated
870 animals released to the wild
4,480 hotline calls answered
612 healthy animals left with their parents thanks to hotline coaching
97 active volunteers gave 11,240 hours
38 school and library visits reached 2,150 students

Slide 4: Our Release Rate, Stated Plainly
Raw release rate: 48% in FY2024, 54% in FY2026
Adjusted to the FY2024 mix of species and injuries: about 49% in FY2026
That is roughly one point of real improvement, not six
Most of the rise came from more orphaned juveniles, which release at high rates
Holding steady and gaining a point while admissions rose 41% with no added staff is still a real result
We do not yet track how animals survive after release; the new enclosure plan addresses this for raptors

Slide 5: The Gap: Raptors
113 raptors admitted in FY2026, mostly red-tailed hawks, barred owls, and American kestrels
We have no enclosure big enough for a hawk or owl to rebuild flight muscle
41 raptors went to Crane Ridge Raptor Center, two hours away, for final conditioning
Each transfer takes a volunteer most of a day and adds stress for the bird
Crane Ridge will limit transfers from outside its region starting in 2027
"Somebody picked up, told me exactly where to drive, and was waiting at the gate with the lights on." (Delia Marsh, Ketterly resident, on bringing us a hawk)

Slide 6: The Project and Its Budget
A 100-foot curved flight enclosure at Bramblecote
Design, site work, and construction: $112,000
Part-time raptor care technician, first year: $28,000
Perches, scales, transport crates, and monitoring cameras: $8,000
Total project cost: $148,000

Slide 7: How the $148,000 Comes Together
Harrow Valley Community Foundation: $60,000, requested today
Individual capital pledges: $52,000, with $38,000 committed and $14,000 still to raise
Ostrander-Bell Family Fund: $36,000, request pending
Other sources total $88,000, of which $38,000 is committed so far
Total: $148,000

Slide 8: What the Enclosure Will Deliver
No more transfers of raptors out of the county once it opens in spring 2027
Hawks and owls released in the county where they were found
A raptor release rate we can measure and report ourselves
A post-release band-return log, so future reports can show what happens after release
A site where our school program can show students what recovery takes
Our request: $60,000 to help build it
